sections.html:
Bartlett is a Chicago-area village split mostly between Cook and DuPage counties, with a small parcel at its western edge in Kane County. The 2020 count was 41,105 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 40,855 is 0.7% lower.

Three counties mean three recorders and three tax offices. The first move in any Bartlett sale is reading the parcel number on your tax bill to learn which one applies.

Most of the population growth came in the 1980s, so the housing is recent compared with the depot-era town center, where the original 1873 station still stands as the Bartlett Depot Museum. The village was incorporated on June 21, 1892. Of 14,522 housing units in the 2020 count, 2.2% were vacant, and the homeowner vacancy rate was 0.9%.

Bartlett leans toward owner-occupied family housing: about 89% of homes are owner-occupied, and 36.6% of households had children under 18 in 2020. That mix means buyers often ask about schools, yards and commute time, so have those answers ready.

Public schools in Bartlett are entirely within Elgin Area School District U46, the second largest district in Illinois. Bartlett High School, Eastview Middle School and elementary schools named Bartlett, Centennial, Sycamore Trails, Prairieview, Nature Ridge and Liberty serve the village, and some students attend South Elgin High School or Kenyon Woods Middle School in South Elgin.

Illinois Route 59 is the main north-south road, with a large retail area at Route 59 and Stearns Road. The Milwaukee District West rail line stops at Bartlett station and runs east to Chicago Union Station, and Pace bus Route 554 connects the village to Elgin and Schaumburg. The mean commute is 29.7 minutes, so buyers who ride the train will ask how far a house is from the platform.

The village's Building Division issues permits for work from decks and pools to driveways and new construction, and inspections by building staff run Monday through Friday only. You can reach the division at 630.540.5920.

The village's rules on new driveways are specific and worth reading before you list a house with a worn drive.

  • The apron, the part of the driveway that meets the street, is the homeowner's responsibility, and the village does not maintain or replace it.
  • Public works inspects the public sidewalk and utilities inside the driveway during permit review. If the sidewalk needs repair the village will do it, which can take up to four weeks and delay the permit.
  • No apron extension is approved when a parkway tree stands within 10 feet of it, and the village will not remove parkway trees for that purpose.
  • If a concrete contractor repairs the public sidewalk, Public Works will reimburse part of the cost. Call 630-837-0811.

Sprinklers and invisible fences placed in the village right-of-way are also the homeowner's problem if sidewalk work damages them. Ask the Building Division for the permit record on your address, and close out any open permit before a buyer's inspector finds it.

County recorders sell the revenue stamps that pay the Illinois transfer tax. Home rule municipalities may add their own tax, so ask the title company whether the village charges one.

The PTAX-203 declaration goes to the county of the parcel. In Cook County the Clerk's deed fee is $107 on the schedule that began April 1, 2024, a sum covering recording, GIS, storage, the state rental housing support fee and a filer fee. Parcels in DuPage or Kane have their own fee lists, so call that recorder.

Ask the title company early which recorder will file your deed, and keep the recorded deed and your copy of the transfer declaration once the county returns them.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale worth considering?
sections.html:
A tidy house can go through a regular listing. A cash offer suits a house needing major work, a move on a deadline, or an estate. The trade is speed and certainty against the higher price a fully updated listing might bring.

  • Get the offer in writing and see who pays closing costs.
  • Name the title company early and learn which recorder will file the deed.
  • Hold on to the recorded deed and your copy of the transfer declaration.

Whichever route you choose, line up the same set of papers: the parcel number, your latest tax bill, any payoff letter from a lender, and the permit record from the Building Division. A buyer who sees those up front tends to close with fewer questions.

Once a contract is signed, the title company orders the search and works out the tax proration for the year. Because the village crosses county lines, the first call is to the recorder that matches your parcel. The seller's side signs the deed and the transfer declaration, the lender, if any, issues a payoff, and the recorder files the deed. Plan for the Building Division to close any open permit before that date, since a permit problem can hold up a buyer's financing or inspection. If the house has a worn driveway apron or a cracked public sidewalk, raise it early and ask Public Works about the reimbursement above rather than leaving it for the buyer.

sections.h2: What to have ready for the title company
sections.html:
Gather the documents a buyer and title company ask for before the contract is even signed. That means your parcel number, the latest tax bill showing the county, any mortgage payoff information, and the permit record for the address. If you finished a basement, built a deck or replaced a driveway, find the permit paperwork and the final inspection, since unfinished items are the ones that surprise buyers.

Ask the title company who pays for the title search and recording, and put the answer in the contract. If you are selling for cash, ask for the offer in writing and compare it with what a listing would net after repairs and fees. If the house is vacant, say so up front, because buyers price in the cost of getting a vacant property ready. A written timeline for closing day, including what happens to utilities and keys, helps both sides avoid confusion.

faqs.q: Which county holds my Bartlett parcel?
faqs.a: Read the parcel number on your tax bill. Bartlett is mostly in Cook and DuPage counties, plus a small piece of Kane. That county's recorder files the deed and its treasurer collects the tax.

faqs.q: What does a deed filing cost at the Cook County Clerk?
faqs.a: $107 on the schedule effective April 1, 2024. It rolls together the county recording fee, a GIS fee, a storage fee, the state rental housing support fee and a filer fee. DuPage and Kane parcels follow those counties' fees.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for a new driveway?
faqs.a: Yes. The Building Division issues driveway permits, and public works reviews the sidewalk and utilities inside the driveway. Sidewalk repair can take up to four weeks and hold up the permit, so apply early and call 630.540.5920.

faqs.q: Who runs the schools in Bartlett?
faqs.a: Elgin Area School District U46, the second largest in Illinois, serves the entire village. Some students attend South Elgin High School instead of Bartlett High School.

faqs.q: May I sell in as-is condition?
faqs.a: Yes, either to a cash buyer or through a listing priced for the condition. Pull your permit record first so nothing surprises the buyer.
